Case Study · 04 · Tre Plus

Built from
nothing

Tre Plus is a Netherlands nearshore product and engineering company operating out of Prishtina. I built the brand from scratch: logo, identity system, website and the full digital experience. The identity was deliberately playful, to separate them from a category that all looks the same, without costing them credibility.

Role
Brand and product designerSole designer, start to finish

Origin
From zeroNo prior brand to work from
Approach

Playful, not unserious

The mark is a plus, drawn as a soft 3D form. It carries the name, works as a graphic device across the site and gives the brand a personality the category rarely has.

Everything around it is restrained: one grotesque, plain layouts, generous space. The colour and the object do the talking, so the credibility never slips.

06

Interface system

The site documented as rules, so it stays consistent without me in the room.

Every element on the page annotated: logo clear space, nav spacing, hero anatomy, the rule that 3D shapes switch colour with the hero keyword.

Each service is bound to one colour and one 3D element. A visitor learns the code once and reads the rest of the site faster because of it.

Labels above fields, required marked, consent before submit, and the send button disabled until valid. Written as rules a developer can build from without asking.

Primary and secondary, four states each, with hex values and spacing. Primary appears once per screen, which is what keeps it meaning something.

01

Three founders, one mark

Two from the Netherlands, one from Kosovo. The symbol is that shape repeated three times and locked together, with the plus sitting in the centre.

02

Orange, for a reason

The primary is Dutch orange. It ties the company to where it sells while staying loud enough to separate it from a category that mostly ships blue.

03

A colour per service

Marketing, design and development each get a colour and a 3D form. It turns the identity into a navigation system rather than decoration.
